notes: Identity verified independently from the supplied canonical text: title Is Implicit Theory of Mind a Real and Robust Phenomenon? Results From a Systematic Replication Study; Louisa Kulke, Britta von Duhn, Dana Schneider, Hannes Rakoczy; DOI 10.1177/0956797617747090. Research Article, Psychological Science, 2018, full 13-page article including methods, results, tables and references; early pagination 1–13 rather than final 888–900. This is a primary replication report, not the original Southgate paper. No PDF was supplied. The neutral description refers to infants, whereas this replication tested adults explicitly using the original paradigm. No target assigned by input order or numeric matching. Candidates, all printed on p. 6: overall DLS t(50) = 1.77, p = .083 (exact), d = 0.25; False Belief 1 t(26) = 4.95, d = 0.95, p < .001 (strict upper bound); False Belief 2 t(23) = −2.64, p = .015 (exact), d = −0.54. These are distinct tests, not interchangeable values. Page 9 Table 2 also reports first-saccade and looking-time outcomes. Numeric fields remain null because the locator does not disambiguate the target. N candidates: p. 6 prints present study n = 54; p. 7 Table 1 explicitly prints N = 51 for Southgate/Senju DLS. The latter supports an overall DLS sample candidate independently, but is a correlation-table sample and does not resolve the requested critical test or the discrepancy with n = 54. No N inferred from degrees of freedom, no group sum, and no effect conversion performed. Reported success mixed is a paradigm-level author narrative: overall findings were not replicated, with False Belief 1 alone replicated; it does not select a specific statistical target.
